A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: Attractions' deployment shows 0 available pods against 1 desired for the whole abnormal window, which points to a pod that is gone. Next I'll confirm against normal, check restarts and uptime, and compare per-endpoint latency across all services.

input.query: SELECT 'n' p, service_name, metric, count(*) c, avg(value) v, min(value) mn, max(value) mx FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.deployment.available','k8s.pod.uptime','k8s.container.restarts') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'a', service_name, metric, count(*), avg(value), min(value), max(value) FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.deployment.available','k8s.pod.uptime','k8s.container.restarts') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Attractions' three Nearby endpoints, which are the normal server-side work, disappear entirely in the abnormal period. Next I'll compare latency per endpoint across periods to see whether other services also changed.

input.reflection: Findings: attractions has zero server spans and zero INFO logs in the abnormal period (normal: ~104 spans, 509 logs), and k8s.deployment.available=0 vs desired=1 for all abnormal samples (normal 1.0). Frontend's calls to attractions (NearbyCinema/Mus/Rest) fail in ~0.015ms with Error status, and frontend /cinema, /museums, /restaurants return HTTP 500 (488 errors total), with matching ERROR logs. Other services (geo, profile, rate, search, reservation, user) show no errors; small latency shifts in rate/reservation with no CPU/memory change, so not treated as separate faults. /hotels and /recommendations stay 200. No hubble network metrics exist. Conclusion: one root cause, attractions pod_unavailable (gone for the whole window, not recovered). Propagation: attractions -> frontend. Frontend is the user-facing tier.
